key_insight: SPG-Layout improves text-driven 3D indoor scene synthesis by combining statistical object priors with a hierarchical large-object-first layout strategy to better handle non-Manhattan geometry.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to generate more physically plausible indoor layouts for robotics, digital twins, and CAD/VR scene design in complex floor plans.
method: Uses statistical priors of object distributions to guide training and improve environmental understanding.
Builds layouts hierarchically, placing large objects first to reduce constraint violations.
Targets both semantic realism and physical plausibility in non-orthogonal indoor spaces.
evidence_signal: The authors introduced a new benchmark of 500 diverse non-Manhattan environments and report consistent improvements over existing methods in both Manhattan and non-Manhattan settings.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the learned priors, so rare room geometries or unusual object arrangements could still be challenging.
paper_title: Text-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis in Non-Manhattan Environments
